metadata.track: qualitative-methodological foundations and evaluation of automated codes/themes
metadata.prisma_counts_for_this_track: not reported; merge with parent database-search exports
metadata.source_policy: Primary papers, official proceedings/publisher pages, and official preprints were used for technical claims. No technical claim in this file is based only on a search-result snippet or abstract.

method_taxonomy.product: reproducibly applied structured codes and commonly topic/domain-summary themes
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: code assignment accuracy, reference construction, prevalence-aware reliability, held-out cases
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: Results do not establish reflexive thematic validity.

method_taxonomy.product: structured codebook or matrix with acknowledged interpretation
method_taxonomy.agreement_role: team consistency can help; reliability is not necessarily truth
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: codebook usability/evolution, matrix and evidence traceability, deliberation, fit to question
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: A shared codebook does not make the analysis non-interpretive.

method_taxonomy.product: researcher-constructed patterns of shared meaning organized around central concepts
method_taxonomy.agreement_role: independent replication, consensus, saturation, and IRR are not universal quality criteria
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: analytic coherence, evidence warrants, reflexivity, depth, alternative readings, negative cases, purpose-fit
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: One consensus theme set is not objective ground truth.

method_taxonomy.product: integrated categories and theory from iterative comparison, memoing, theoretical sampling, and category development
method_taxonomy.agreement_role: early codes are usually interim analytic devices
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: constant comparison, memo/category provenance, theoretical sampling, relationships, theory development
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: Open coding alone is not grounded theory; axial coding is not universal across GT schools.

method_taxonomy.product: systematic contextual classification into conventional, directed, or summative categories
method_taxonomy.agreement_role: coding-scheme transparency and conditional reliability can be relevant
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: category definition/exhaustiveness, contextual classification, inductive additions, distinction between counting and interpretation
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: Keyword counts alone are not qualitative interpretation.

method_taxonomy.product: case-by-code matrix retaining case context, using deductive, inductive, or mixed coding
method_taxonomy.agreement_role: structured comparison is expected but remains interpretive
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: source pointers, matrix cells, case context, codebook versions, analytic decisions
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: Iterative coding does not by itself imply grounded theory.

method_taxonomy.product: focused templates, matrices, and synthesis for time-sensitive questions, sometimes without formal coding
method_taxonomy.agreement_role: fit to purpose and expertise matter more than speed alone
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: decision-relevant findings, omissions, contextual fidelity, verification workload, time/cost
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: Faster output is not automatically equivalent or better.

method_taxonomy.product: labels, snippets, clusters, or categories without an explicit qualitative methodology/end product
method_taxonomy.agreement_role: label agreement may be an appropriate task metric
method_taxonomy.automation_evaluation: classification and label quality under an explicitly limited claim
method_taxonomy.do_not_infer: The words inductive, open, or themes do not establish RTA or GT.

metric_construct_assessments.operation: exact/fuzzy lexical overlap, ROUGE, BLEU, METEOR
metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: insufficient for interpretive equivalence or evidentiary validity; configuration and polarity failures are documented
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: task-specific expert validation and sensitivity to reference wording/configuration

metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: not originally validated for qualitative theme equivalence; can miss conceptual matches or reward broad topical similarity
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: expert theme-pair/set judgments, threshold calibration, held-out domain tests, contradiction cases

metric_construct_assessments.intended_construct: parsimonious alignment of similarly granular sets
metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: penalizes legitimate splits/merges and contradicts interpretive many-to-many structure
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: compare one-to-one and many-to-many results; report unmatched items and granularity

metric_construct_assessments.intended_construct: partial accommodation of theme splits, merges, and granularity
metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: structurally preferable in some tasks but still embedding- and threshold-dependent
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: human conceptual matching, threshold sweep, uncertainty and disagreement

metric_construct_assessments.operation: coverage/recall against a reference or Aggregate Code Space
metric_construct_assessments.intended_construct: recovery of concepts in the represented reference space
metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: cannot recover concepts missed by all analysts and need not measure participant spread or evidentiary coverage
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: multiple situated analysts, participant/source coverage, negative cases, omissions audit

metric_construct_assessments.intended_construct: difference from a reference or pooled code distribution
metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: difference is ambiguous between valuable standpoint, granularity, and unsupported invention
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: expert warrant review and source-level evidence audit

metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: can reward generic topical clusters and penalize complex themes that connect tension or contradiction
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: contrast with expert depth/warrant judgments and adversarial counterexamples

metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: does not establish validity; stable systematic bias is possible
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: crossed perturbations and substantive expert adjudication, not lexical similarity alone

metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: necessary for audit but does not establish representativeness, interpretive warrant, or omitted evidence
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: exactness, entailment, omission, participant-spread, and audit-completion tests

metric_construct_assessments.validity_assessment: susceptible to order, verbosity, self-enhancement and same-family preference; general NLG validation does not transfer automatically
metric_construct_assessments.validation_required: independent families, randomized order, repeat runs, blinded expert calibration, agreement and error analysis

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Chen et al. (2026). A Computational Method for Measuring ‘Open Codes’ in Qualitative Analysis. Findings of ACL 2026, 41740–41758.
metrics: coefficient of variation across ten runs
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: No singular correct answer is assumed. Ten-run rankings were stable in the tested setting; synthetic edge-case and hallucination tests reveal distinct metric responses.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: A pooled reference is better than a single gold but remains bounded by observed coders and LLM-mediated merging. Stability is not validity; divergence may be valuable.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Zhong, M., Wang, P., and Field, A. (2025). HICode: Hierarchical Inductive Coding with LLMs. EMNLP 2025, 31060–31078.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: hierarchical code/theme induction with reference matching
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Human and cosine matching diverged; human alpha was .31. HICode human P/R .72/.74 versus cosine .53/.51; TopicGPT human .18/.33 versus cosine .04/.49.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Many-to-many topology helps granularity, but the reference remains privileged and cosine thresholds miss conceptual equivalence.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Parfenova et al. (2025). Text Annotation via Inductive Coding: Comparing Human Experts to LLMs in Qualitative Data Analysis. Findings of NAACL 2025.
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Three experts assessed 15 sentences; reported alpha .2. Alternatives can be preferred despite lower reference similarity.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Single-reference proximity does not capture interpretive depth; human sample is too small for broad validity claims.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Dai, S.-C., Xiong, A., and Ku, L.-W. (2023). LLM-in-the-loop: Leveraging Large Language Model for Thematic Analysis. Findings of EMNLP 2023.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: human–LLM codebook construction and coding-reliability assignment
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Human–machine kappa .87/.81; original human agreement .66/.77; cosine .886/.890; accuracy .84/.83.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: The LLM co-constructs the reference, so agreement is not an independent inductive-discovery test and does not establish RTA validity.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Rao et al. (2025). QuaLLM: An LLM-based Framework to Extract Quantitative Insights from Online Forums. Findings of NAACL 2025.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: hybrid computational content analysis using an external topic taxonomy
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Two researchers jointly evaluated 125 submissions/2,511 comments; a three-annotator 100-sample check reports kappa .59/.63 human and .54/.61 human–LLM.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Reported coverage is topic coverage, not participant or meaning coverage; deductive label agreement does not validate RTA.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Xu et al. (2026). TAMA: A Human-AI Collaborative Thematic Analysis Framework Using Multi-Agent LLMs for Clinical Interviews.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: multi-agent coding-reliability/codebook TA with expert stopping
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Twelve consensus human themes from three analysts; G-Eval plateaued and over-refined, requiring expert stopping; quote judge tested on one transcript.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: methods, evaluation, results, limitations, metric appendices
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: The Jaccard label is mathematically inaccurate; hit rate ignores extra themes; coherence can reward topical homogeneity; same-family judging and reference-construction overlap limit independence.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Yi et al. (2025). Auto-TA: Towards Scalable Automated Thematic Analysis (TA) via Multi-Agent Large Language Models with Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:2506.23998v2.
automated_qualitative_studies.status: arXiv preprint; other publication/peer-review status not independently verified
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: multi-agent end-to-end theme generation with lexical repeatability diagnostics
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Audit log and quote IDs are supplied; authors acknowledge multiple valid theme sets, expertise, prompt sensitivity, and low lexical similarity for valid outputs.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: evaluation metric definitions and limitations, arXiv v2
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: All three trustworthiness labels are construct-misaligned: quote reuse, wording stability, and within-corpus subset similarity are not the qualitative constructs named.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Yi et al. (2025). SFT-TA: Supervised Fine-Tuned Agents in Multi-Agent LLMs for Automated Inductive Thematic Analysis. arXiv:2509.17167v1.
automated_qualitative_studies.status: inspected PDF says PMLR/ML4H 2025 with volume XXX; final bibliographic and peer-review status not reported
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: fine-tuning toward a fixed 12-theme reference universe
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Ten reference themes train and two validate, each with 30 human-reviewed LLM paraphrases; all 12 references are then used for best matching.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: methods, evaluation and appendices, arXiv v1
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Direct reference leakage/alignment prevents a generalization claim; human IRR/statistics are not reported; same-family judge circularity remains.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Yi et al. (2025). Position: Thematic Analysis of Unstructured Clinical Transcripts with Large Language Models. arXiv:2509.14597v2.
automated_qualitative_studies.status: arXiv/workshop position paper; peer-review status not reported
automated_qualitative_studies.claimed_method: evaluation framework for clinical thematic analysis
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: unvalidated metric proposal and landscape review
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Proposal only; no empirical framework validation in the inspected version.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: methods review and proposed-framework sections, arXiv v2
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: One-to-one matching conflicts with acknowledged many-to-many interpretations; its description of RTA imports consensus/reliability procedures.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Yi et al. (2026). Automated Thematic Analysis for Clinical Qualitative Data: Iterative Codebook Refinement with Full Provenance. arXiv:2603.08989v1.
automated_qualitative_studies.status: arXiv preprint; manuscript states submission to AMIA 2026, acceptance not verified
automated_qualitative_studies.claimed_method: iterative thematic analysis with full provenance
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: persistent evidence graph and action ledger with automated refinement
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Persistent IDs link transcript turns, chunks, quotes, codes, subthemes and themes; ledger records action, role, input/output, justification and timestamp.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: architecture, metrics, experiments and limitations, arXiv v1
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Strong process traceability, but provenance is not validity. Same-family judge bias, topical cosine, abstraction, post-hoc iteration, and metric overlap are acknowledged.

automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: iterative constraint/rubric refinement with LLM judging
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Three experts reached rubric kappa .78. On 300 code judgments from one expert, reported judge accuracy was 90%, expert accuracy 89%, and kappa .68; quality peaked near ten iterations.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: rubric construction, judge validation, experiments and limitations
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Explicit rubric is a strength; binary constraints are coarse, one expert/domain underlies main validation, and judge-model independence is not reported.

automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: row/segment processing with complete configuration and output logs
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Two GPT-5.2 passes over 23 transcripts reached kappa 1.0 for binary coding but showed systematic excess mentions versus a published human codebook.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: system, case-study and limitation sections, arXiv v1
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Direct counterexample to stability=validity; atomistic context and whether humans actually inspect logs remain limitations.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Jowsey et al. (2025). Frankenstein, thematic analysis and generative AI. PLOS ONE, 20(9), e0330217.
automated_qualitative_studies.claimed_method: comparison of generative AI and published thematic analyses
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: first-output Copilot comparison and exact quote audit across five datasets
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Correct quotes: human 79.1% (SD 27.1), Copilot 36.0% (SD 43.4). Fabricated Copilot quotes: 57.5% (SD 44.5). Evidence was concentrated early in documents.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Strong source-fidelity evidence; one minimally prompted proprietary assistant and heterogeneous TA traditions limit generalization. Detailed text has a conflicting 44.5% fabrication value; table/abstract support 57.5%.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Hill et al. (2026). Large language models for thematic analysis in healthcare research: A blinded mixed-methods comparison. PLOS Digital Health, 5(4), e0001189.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: coding-reliability/codebook evaluation with adjudicated reference and IRR
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: One seven-participant focus group. Deductive human/LLM agreement 92.7/93.5%, kappa .34/.34, AC1 .92/.93; only GPT-5 non-inferior inductively. Strict/expanded/comprehensive hallucination 1.2/8.6/12.4%.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: methods, results, qualitative comparison and limitations
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Reference/IRR procedure is incongruent with RTA label; low prevalence explains kappa paradox; one qualitative rater and one transcript limit inductive validity.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Montes et al. (2025). Large Language Models in Thematic Analysis: Prompt Engineering, Evaluation, and Guidelines. arXiv:2510.18456v1.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: prompt-tuned code/theme generation and human preference/rubric comparison
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: LLM preferred 61%, human 37%; only five complete agreements; no IRR statistic. Latent-semantic interpretation was weakest (weighted average 2.59).
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: methodology, results and limitations, arXiv v1
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Best pipeline and prompts were selected on the same corpus; no held-out data or run stability; preference does not establish method-valid RTA.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Perez, N., Bhaduri, S., and Chadha, A. (2026). Position: A Semiotic-Hermeneutic Approach to Qualitative Evaluation of LLMs with an Inductive Conceptual Rating Metric. GEM 2026, 1036–1047.
automated_qualitative_studies.status: peer-reviewed ACL Anthology workshop/proceedings position paper
automated_qualitative_studies.claimed_method: reflexive/inductive content analysis and Inductive Conceptual Rating
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: manual concept inventories and comparison against a situated human baseline
metrics: ten model runs with modal output selection
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Five open-survey datasets; human and LLM concept inventories are manually aligned.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: metric definition and experimental sections, pp. 1036–1047
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: With the union of observed concepts as the universe, true negatives cannot occur; ICR accuracy reduces to Jaccard after manual alignment. Human coder count/expertise/IRR not reported.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: AlGhamdi (2026). From Code Variability to Theme Convergence: Evaluating Large Language Models Against Human Thematic Analysis. International Journal of Qualitative Methods, 25.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: coding-reliability comparison with one historical analysis
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Code F1 55.9–87.6; theme agreement 90.9–100; structured code average 83.1 versus general prompt 59.2; inter-session theme average 86.1.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: One reference interpretation, public-thesis contamination risk, one system/four sessions, and F1 not measuring depth/reflexivity are acknowledged. Exact match-adjudication independence not reported.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Pi et al. (2026). A Landscape of Computational Approaches to Qualitative Analysis. arXiv:2601.11739v1.
automated_qualitative_studies.operationalized_method: M1–M4 meaning-depth and D1–D4 model-form taxonomy
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Separates manifest description, categorical themes, latent interpretation, and theory-mediated meaning; argues evaluation must change with claim depth.
automated_qualitative_studies.evidence_location: taxonomy, evaluation and research-agenda sections, arXiv v1
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Useful novelty collision and conceptual framework, but not an empirically validated benchmark.

automated_qualitative_studies.citation: Bedemariam et al. (2025). Potential and Perils of Large Language Models as Judges of Unstructured Textual Data. arXiv:2501.08167.
automated_qualitative_studies.principal_evidence: Human–model agreement 76–79%, kappa .34–.44, ordinal alpha .49–.60; model–model agreement often higher.
automated_qualitative_studies.construct_validity: Assesses internal alignment of generated artifacts, not fidelity/coverage against the full corpus. Human judge count/expertise not reported; judges over-rate topical similarity.

scoring.2: adequate for the study's stated claim

quality_rubric.instruction: Report dimensions separately; do not sum into a simplistic best-study ranking.
dimensions: qualified blinded human evaluation with disagreement/uncertainty
proportionality of claims including verification burden
interpretation_blocking_flags: RTA validity claimed solely from consensus or IRR
same-family judge presented as independent truth without calibration

no source-level evidence access for a fidelity claim

candidate_gaps.gap: method-aware evaluation without a unique gold interpretation
candidate_gaps.unresolved: No inspected work empirically validates one portfolio across coding-reliability, codebook and reflexive analytic contracts.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: preregistered method-specific tasks, multiple situated analysts, expert construct validation, and rank-change analysis

candidate_gaps.gap: validated semantic equivalence for code/theme sets
candidate_gaps.unresolved: No cross-domain threshold/topology validation for interpretive equivalence, splits/merges and contradiction.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: expert pair/set judgments with rationales, held-out domains/models, threshold sensitivity and ambiguity reporting

candidate_gaps.unresolved: No inspected system integrates participant spread, rare/negative cases, contradictions and unsupported synthesis end to end.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: participant-linked corpora, stratified rare-case recall, adversarial tests and qualitative expert review

candidate_gaps.unresolved: Inspectability is improved, but representation and warrants are not validated.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: machine-checkable provenance plus independent stratified audits of exactness, entailment, omission, spread and audit usability

candidate_gaps.unresolved: Most studies vary one factor or equate lexical repeatability with quality.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: crossed seed by prompt by order by sample by model by analyst variance decomposition with substantive adjudication

candidate_gaps.gap: independent LLM-judge validation for qualitative output
candidate_gaps.unresolved: Calibration samples are small and same-family dependence remains.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: blinded multi-expert judgment sample, multiple independent judge families, randomized order, adversarial cases and error analysis

candidate_gaps.gap: prospective workflow value and verification burden
candidate_gaps.unresolved: Preference and similarity rarely include verification, correction, reflexive labor or downstream decisions.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: prospective no-AI and constrained-assistant arms measuring time by stage, edits, errors, depth and downstream use

candidate_gaps.unresolved: No validated benchmark evaluates warrants and alternative readings rather than wording overlap.
candidate_gaps.minimum_evidence: competing readings and counterevidence with expert assessment of warrants, theory fit, alternatives and harm

screening_recommendations.important_rule: Methodological incongruence is not itself an exclusion reason; code claimed and operationalized methodology separately.

limitations: Single-reviewer methodological track; no independent duplicate screening.
The web-search interface did not expose stable result counts, so this track does not independently support PRISMA numerators.
Forward/backward chaining was targeted rather than demonstrably exhaustive.
Publication status for several 2025–2026 manuscripts was not verified beyond the inspected version.
Private datasets prevent source-level replication in several studies.
Construct critiques are reviewer interpretations grounded in cited definitions and methods, not necessarily author-stated limitations.
